content: The NCLEX-PN (National Council Licensure Examination-Practical Nurse) is a computer-adaptive test designed to evaluate the entry-level nursing competence of candidates. Passing this examination is a mandatory requirement for individuals seeking licensure as a Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) or Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) in all U.S. states and territories. These territories include American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, and the Virgin Islands. The NCLEX-PN, along with the NCLEX-RN (for registered nurses), is developed and owned by the National Council of State Boards of Nursing, Inc. (NCSBN). The purpose of these examinations is to ensure public safety by assessing whether candidates possess the knowledge, skills, and abilities essential for the safe and effective practice of nursing at the entry level. The NCLEX examinations are administered in a computerized adaptive testing (CAT) format, which combines modern computer technology with advanced measurement theory to enhance the efficiency of the testing process. These exams are currently delivered by Pearson VUE at their network of Pearson Professional Centers (PPC). The CAT format adjusts the difficulty of questions based on the test-taker's performance, ensuring a tailored and precise assessment of their abilities. The NCLEX uses a variety of question types, including single-response multiple-choice, multiple-response, fill-in-the-blank, drag-and-drop, and others. Additionally, the exam incorporates diverse display formats such as charts, exhibits, tables, and graphic images. All test items are meticulously developed and validated by practicing nurses, educators, and regulators from across the country. The content of the exam is based on a practice analysis conducted every three years to ensure its relevance and alignment with current nursing practices. The majority of the test items are designed to assess application-level or higher cognitive skills, although the exam may include questions spanning all cognitive levels. This ensures a comprehensive evaluation of the candidate's ability to apply knowledge in practical and clinical scenarios.
